questions.q: What is the purpose of a customer profile class?
options: It is a template of default values (credit limit, terms, dunning, statement cycle) assigned to many accounts at once
It is a security role that limits which users can view a customer
It is a type of receivables activity
It replaces the need for a customer account entirely
questions.explain: A profile class bundles common defaults so they don't need to be configured individually on every customer account.

questions.q: Can an individual customer account override a value inherited from its profile class?
options: No, profile class values are permanent and uneditable per account
Yes, the profile provides defaults, and individual accounts can override specific values
Only the credit limit can ever be overridden
Only a system administrator can override any profile value, never a user
questions.explain: The profile class is a starting point. Any account can have specific values, like credit limit or payment terms, overridden individually.

questions.q: What typically happens when a new transaction would push a customer's open balance over their credit limit?
options: The transaction is permanently deleted
The customer's account is automatically closed
The transaction can be flagged for a credit hold, pending manual review and release
Nothing — credit limits are purely informational and never enforced
questions.explain: Exceeding the credit limit commonly triggers a hold rather than an outright block, keeping the decision in the hands of a credit analyst.

questions.q: In the Harborline Retail Group example, what was the customer's credit limit and projected balance after the new $11,000 invoice?
options: Limit $42,000, projected balance $50,000
Limit $53,000, projected balance $42,000
Limit $11,000, projected balance $42,000
Limit $50,000, projected balance $53,000
questions.explain: Harborline's existing $42,000 open balance plus the new $11,000 invoice totals $53,000, which exceeds its $50,000 credit limit.

questions.q: Besides credit limit, name another attribute commonly set at the profile class level.
options: The statement cycle and dunning plan
The company's chart of accounts structure
The ledger currency
The AutoInvoice grouping rule
questions.explain: Profile classes also commonly default the statement cycle, dunning/collections plan, payment terms, and discrepancy tolerance.
